```{r}
#| label: library
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3)
library(housepi)
housepi_theme_set()
set.seed(42)
```

Time dependent transmission models require a choice for the infectivity profile $f$, defined as the instantaneous risk of secondary infection associated to a reference infector.
An infectivity profile is thus a function of the time from infection $t_{i}$ to transmission at time $t$, the "generation time" $t - t_{i}$. Eventually, the profile could depend on other infector covariates.

In certain applications a profile has to be expressed as a function of the time from symptoms onset $t_{i}^{(\rm ons)}$ to transmission. In such cases, the profile will be a function of the generation time and of the incubation period $\tau_{i}^{(\rm inc)}$ of the infector, remembering that $t_{i} + \tau_{i}^{(\rm inc)} = t_{i}^{(\rm ons)}$.

Note that for technical reasons, infectivity profiles in housepi can only depend on covariates of the infector, and not of the infectee. This prevents from using directly quantities as the "serial time" (the time between symptom onsets of infector and infectee) and workarounds need to be implemented manually.

In short, assuming $i$ the infector and $k$ the infectee, the time intervals supported by the infectivity profiles in housepi are

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center;">
<div style="white-space: nowrap;">

| Time Interval |  | Profile | Support |
|---------------|--|---------|:-------:|
| Generation | $t_{k} - t_{i}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i})$ | <span style="color: green;">&check;</span> |
| Onset to Transmission | $t_{k} - t_{i}^{(\rm ons)}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i}\vert \tau_{i}^{(\rm inc)})$ | <span style="color: green;">&check;</span> |
| Serial | $t_{k}^{(\rm ons)} - t_{i}^{(\rm ons)}$ | $f(t_{k} - t_{i}\vert \tau_{i}^{(\rm inc)}, \tau_{k}^{(\rm inc)})$ | <span style="color: red;">&cross;</span> |

</div>
</div>

According to this scheme, infectivity profile definitions can be of two kinds:

* **Generic**: if all individuals in the study share the same profile;
* **Augmented**: if profile depends on individual covariates.

At any time one can provide a custom choice for the profile, however all models requiring profiles will have a templated infectivity definition incorporated.
For example, consider the model "augmented infection time" introduced in [Get started](housepi.html).
The model template comes in continuous time and with a templated generic profile which is chosen to be a gamma distribution parametrized with `mean` and `var`:

```{r}
#| label: load-continuous-profile
hhcontinuos <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  new_housepi_model("augmented infection time")
# extract current loaded profile definitions
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhcontinuos)
# display definitions
defs
# display function arguments
defs$func_args
```

Here we accessed the definition associated to the model by calling `get_infec_profile`. We can "expose" the behaviour of housepi functions by calling `expose_infec_profile`. This will generate an object holding the infectivity profile definitions to be used to compute instantaneous and cumulative values of the profile

```{r}
#| label: plot-continuous-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation time in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args)

library(ggplot2)

# function to plot a demonstration of both instantaneous and cumulative profiles
plot_profile_demo <- function(profile,
                              color_inst = "black",
                              color_cumul = "coral") {
  infec <- dplyr::tibble(gentime = seq(0, 100, 0.05),
                         inst = profile$inst(gentime),
                         cumul = profile$cumul(gentime))
  # coefficient to re-scale the cumulative
  rescale <- max(infec$cumul) / max(infec$inst)

  ggplot(infec, aes(x = gentime)) +
    # plot cumulative profile
    theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = color_cumul),
          axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = color_cumul),
          axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = color_cumul)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = color_cumul) +
    # plot instantaneous
    geom_line(aes(y = inst), color = color_inst) +
    # apply rescaling
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Instantaneous",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "Cumulative")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Generation Time") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10))
}

# plot instantaneous and cumulative profile
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

# Discrete time models

To move to discrete time we need to specify it at the moment of the model generation by adding the option `discr = TRUE`.
This model requires compilation as for all custom models.

```{r}
#| label: load-discrete-model
hhdiscrete <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  new_housepi_model("augmented infection time",
                    discr = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

Keep in mind that for discrete time infectivity profiles, we truncate by default by setting `min = 1`.
This is done to avoid transmission to occur on day 0 of infection.
The discrete profile is now a discretized gamma with the same parameters^[Since the distribution is truncated the actual mean value will typically be different than the parameter `mean`.].

```{r}
#| label: plot-discrete-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Discrete instantaneous infectivity profile as a function of the generation day in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args, discr = TRUE)
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

# Custom infectivity profiles

Imagine we would like to associate a gamma distribution as infectivity profile.
In this simple hypothesis all individuals will share the same profile which depends only on the generation time.
We can provide a custom infectivity profile calling `add_infec_profile()` as follows:

```{r}
#| label: add-custom-profile
hhdiscrete <- hhdiscrete |>
  add_infec_profile("gamma", shape = 4, scale = 1.3)
defs <- get_infec_profile(hhdiscrete)
defs
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-custom-profile
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Custom discrete instantaneous infectivity profile in black.
#|  On a second axis in orange, the corresponding cumulative infectivity profile.
profile <- expose_infec_profile(defs$func, defs$func_args, discr = TRUE)
plot_profile_demo(profile)
```

If the profiles, distributions or functions currently loaded in housepi are not sufficient to deal with your case study, we provide a mechanism to define custom user functions^[Unfortunately, this requires some programming knowledge in C++.].
We show how to deal with [user functions](user_functions.html) in the namesake vignette.
